title: The anatomy of performance: can Oxford find a way to measure the thrill of driving?
summary: Together with researchers from the SDG Impact Lab at the University of Oxford, we set out to better understand the thrill of driving and explore whether it can be measured. The anatomy of performance follows that work across four episodes.
body_markdown:
There’s quite a lot going on in a single lap. Sensors measure heart rate, changes in sweating, eye movements, and brain activity. Meanwhile, the cars record acceleration, braking, steering, and the forces experienced through corners.


Between driving segments, participants rate how they feel. Afterwards, they describe the experience in interviews. A pounding heart tells us something, but it doesn’t tell us whether someone’s enjoying themselves.


That’s why researchers from the SDG Impact Lab at the University of Oxford bring these measurements together: to explore what contributes to the thrill of driving and test whether that experience can be meaningfully measured.
